candidates.title: Integration-binary fixture prelude (make_bus / make_hydro / identity_correlation) re-authored byte-for-byte across the par integration binaries with no shared tests/common

evidence.command: diff <(git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/tests/forward_sampler.rs | sed -n '74,122p') <(git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/tests/conformance.rs | sed -n '61,109p'); diff <(git show a136840d:.../forward_sampler.rs | sed -n '61,72p') <(git show a136840d:.../conformance.rs | sed -n '23,34p'); git ls-tree a136840d -- crates/cobre-stochastic/tests; git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/Cargo.toml | grep -nA4 '[features]'
evidence.output: make_hydro diff: EMPTY (byte-identical ~49-line Hydro literal, 16 HydroPenalties fields all 0.0 + inflow_nonnegativity_cost:1000.0, declare_mirror_unit_group(EntityId(0))). make_bus diff: EMPTY (byte-identical 11-line Bus literal). identity_correlation diff: only param name `ids` vs `entity_ids` (29-line CorrelationModel literal otherwise identical). tests/ dir has 8 flat *.rs binaries and NO common/ module. Cargo.toml [features] declares only `slow-tests = []` (no test-support feature). Spread map: make_bus/make_hydro/make_inflow_model/identity_correlation present in forward_sampler, conformance, halton_integration, sobol_integration, lhs_integration, reproducibility (6 binaries); identity_correlation also in saa_golden_value (7).
evidence.reading: The two par integration binaries in scope re-declare the same entity-construction prelude verbatim; make_stage is the only per-family divergence (forward_sampler `(index,id,bf,method)` vs conformance `(index,id,branching_factor)`), matching the yardstick's observation that only make_stage_* differs per family. There is no crate-local tests/common and no test-support feature, so the prelude is copy-pasted per file. A field added to Hydro/Bus/CorrelationModel must be hand-propagated to every copy; the yardstick §3.1.4 praises exactly the O(1) field-add builder that today lives only in cobre-sddp/tests/common.

candidates.fixShape: Introduce a single shared fixture surface for the crate's cobre-core entity builders and mod-declare it once per binary, so make_bus/make_hydro/make_inflow_model/identity_correlation are authored once. Roadmap-consistent options: (a) low-risk interim — a crate-local `tests/common/` module (the yardstick §5.1 interim state before test-support collapse), each binary `mod common;` then `use crate::common::*`; (b) the yardstick's target — hoist the cobre-core entity builders behind a `test-support` cargo feature so the builders live with the type they build (§5.2). Because these construct cobre-core types (Hydro/Bus/InflowModel/CorrelationModel), cobre-core's test-support surface is the durable home; the crate-local tests/common is the safe first step. Keep the per-family make_stage variants as thin overrides. Neutral to the layering (test infra only); introduces no new production abstraction, so no one-consumer-abstraction conflict. Cross-reference the mirror `Oracle test-harness duplication` entry rather than restating it, and note the wider halton/sobol/lhs/reproducibility/saa spread is owned by the tree-noise substation and the crate-wide total by the test-corpus station.

candidates.title: Inline/sibling unit-test fixture builders (Stage / InflowModel) re-authored across ~9 par test sites with make_model byte-identical between precompute.rs and evaluate.rs

evidence.command: diff <(git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/precompute.rs | sed -n '653,669p') <(git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/evaluate.rs | sed -n '515,531p'); for f in aggregate closure contribution evaluate lag_kernel lag_transition precompute validation; do grep -c 'fn make_stage\|fn make_model\|fn make_inflow_model' <(git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/$f.rs); done
evidence.output: make_model precompute.rs:653 vs evaluate.rs:515 diff: EMPTY (byte-identical 6-arg InflowModel builder, `annual: None`). make_stage precompute.rs:628 vs evaluate.rs:490: identical except `NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(...).unwrap()` vs local `dummy_date(...)` wrapper of the same call. Per-file builder census in par/: precompute(make_stage x3, make_model x2), evaluate(make_stage x1, make_model x1), validation(make_model x2 incl make_model_with_annual), aggregate(make_stage x1). validation make_model hardcodes mean_m3s:100.0; aggregate make_stage uses duration 720.0/branching_factor 1 vs precompute/evaluate 744.0/10 — same Stage struct, same StageStateConfig/block_mode/risk_config/ScenarioSourceConfig boilerplate, differing only in a couple of default literals.
evidence.reading: Every par unit-test module rebuilds the same two cobre-core structs from scratch. precompute and evaluate carry a genuinely identical make_model; the make_stage copies differ only in default constants, not shape. There is no shared O(1)-field-add Stage/InflowModel builder in this crate (it exists only in cobre-sddp/tests/common), so a field added to Stage or InflowModel must be edited in every copy — the fixture-fragmentation cost the yardstick §3.2.3 names. Distinct location from the integration-prelude finding (src/ unit tests vs tests/ binaries), same root cause and same fix surface.

candidates.fixShape: Provide one parameterized builder each for Stage and InflowModel (the O(1) field-add builder pattern the yardstick §3.1.4 credits to cobre-sddp/tests/common/builders.rs), reachable from both the inline unit tests and the integration binaries via the crate test-support surface proposed in the companion finding; each existing make_stage/make_model becomes a thin wrapper that overrides only the defaults it cares about (duration, branching_factor, mean). Delete the byte-identical make_model copy pair outright. Keeps every test body and assertion unchanged (a refactor, not a coverage change); neutral to layering; no new production abstraction.

candidates.title: simulate_two_season_par2 PAR(2) Box-Muller scenario simulator duplicated byte-for-byte across the two par/fitting sibling test files

evidence.output: The two 35-line bodies are identical except the LCG state variable is named `lcg_state` in tests.rs and `lcg` in estimation/tests.rs. Both use the same LCG multiplier 6_364_136_223_846_793_005 / increment 1_442_695_040_888_963_407, the same burnin=200, the same >>11 / (1u64<<53) uniform, the same Box-Muller `(-2*ln u1).sqrt()*cos(2*PI*u2)`, and the same `values[i] = phi_1*values[i-1] + phi_2*values[i-2] + noise` recurrence, returning the identical (obs_s0, obs_s1) two-season split. Both files are the sibling tests.rs for par/fitting.
evidence.reading: A non-trivial deterministic PAR(2) generator (the seed source for the roundtrip and PACF analytical tests in both files) is maintained in two places that differ only by a cosmetic rename; a change to the noise generator in one silently diverges from the other, weakening the shared-seed contract both rely on.

candidates.fixShape: Hoist the one simulator into a single shared par/fitting test helper that both sibling files import (a `#[cfg(test)]` helper module under par/fitting/, or the crate test-support surface if the companion findings introduce it), and delete the copy. Behavior-neutral; the generated series is identical by construction so no golden/assertion changes. Neutral to layering.

candidates.title: pop_mean_std and pop_mean_std_ann are identical population mean/std helpers declared twice in the same file (par/fitting/tests.rs)

evidence.output: Diff is a single line: `fn pop_mean_std(...)` vs `fn pop_mean_std_ann(...)`. The 11-line bodies are byte-identical: n<1 -> (0,0); mean = sum/n; n<2 -> (mean,0); population variance sum((x-mean)^2)/n; return (mean, var.sqrt()).
evidence.reading: Two identically-bodied helpers coexist in one file, separated only by an `_ann` suffix on the name; the `_ann` copy adds no annual-specific behavior. Pure duplication with zero divergence — one helper serves both call sites.

candidates.fixShape: Delete pop_mean_std_ann and point its call sites at the single pop_mean_std (or, if these move under the consolidated par/fitting test helper, keep one copy there). Behavior-neutral; identical output. Neutral to layering.
